fields.sections.0.h: The Beginning of a Bizarre Search Experience
fields.sections.4.h: Unnecessary AI Imposition by Tech Companies
fields.sections.5.h: Paradox: Is Technological Progress a Counterintuitive Regression?
fields.sections.0.ko: The author experienced a strange response from Google while searching for basketball-related memes. When Dario Šaric, a Philadelphia 76ers draft pick in 2014, did not come to the United States until completing his contract in Turkey, fans joked that he "could never come." The author simply entered a search query to find past tweets or posts addressing this meme.
fields.sections.1.ko: Google misunderstood the user's search intent. Upon seeing the search terms, it determined that the user had been rejected by some man in life and offered to play the role of an empathetic digital friend. What the user wanted was simply past web links, but in 2026, Google does not work that way. Even expanding the AI Summary (AI Overview) made the situation more strange.
fields.sections.2.ko: The author poses a fundamental question: Is it truly the search engine's role to comfort users and listen empathetically? How does this align with Google's core mission to "organize the world's information and make it universally accessible and useful"? The author believes this would be acceptable if it were a separate chat-based app (Gemini), but as behavior in the search bar, it is inappropriate. This is a strong criticism that Google has lost its original purpose.
fields.sections.3.ko: Paradoxically, the actual information the author wanted already existed hundreds of pixels below the AI Summary after scrolling. In other words, Google's existing search function worked accurately, but the AI layer overlaid on top interfered with user experience. This demonstrates that AI technology adoption hinders rather than improves search quality.
fields.sections.4.ko: The author reaches a sobering conclusion. Regardless of one's views on AI or chatbots themselves, Google's current behavior is simply strange. Is it normal to force users into continuously dependent conversational relationships with computers? If many aspects of search worked well before LLMs, why must everything be overlaid with AI? This is presented as a concrete example of how major technology corporations damage user experience while following business trends.
fields.sections.5.ko: The author's final phrase is cynical. It ends with Google suggesting that it would speak to the user as an old friend who has always looked out for them. This suggests how awkward and inconvenient the redefinition of human-machine relationships pursued by tech companies feels from the user's perspective. The core message is not that AI technology itself is bad, but rather a challenge to the manner in which it is forcibly inserted into unnecessary places.
fields.caveat: This piece is an opinion based on one individual's specific experience and does not prove that Google's AI Overview feature produces uniformly negative effects across all searches.
